Understanding Async Await in JavaScript

Asynchronous programming in JavaScript is traditionally powered by callbacks and Promises. With ES2017, the async/await syntax was introduced to write asynchronous code that reads like synchronous code.

The Async Keyword

Putting the async keyword before a function declaration automatically wraps its return value in a resolved Promise. It also unlocks the usage of the await expression inside the function body.

Error Handling with Try Catch

One of the primary benefits of async/await is that synchronous try...catch blocks can be used to catch rejected promises without requiring chained .catch() handlers.
